claim: Let \(C_n^k\) be the \(k\)-th power of the cycle on \(\mathbb Z_n\). For every noncomplete Dirac cycle power, equivalently \(\lceil n/4\rceil\le k<\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), one has \(\operatorname{rc}(C_n^k)=\operatorname{src}(C_n^k)=2\). If \(n<4k\), a generator-based two-coloring exists: color the edges of cyclic distance \(k\) red and all shorter generator edges blue. At the exact boundary \(n=4k\), no two-coloring depending only on cyclic distance can be rainbow connecting, but the following non-generator-based coloring is strongly rainbow connecting: write each edge uniquely as \(\{i,i+r\}\) with \(1\le r\le k\) modulo \(4k\), and color it by the parity of \(\lfloor i/k\rfloor\). Complete cycle powers have \(\operatorname{rc}=\operatorname{src}=1\).
integrity: The infinite statement is proved analytically. Finite computation is used only as a stress test. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats cycle powers only, not all Dirac circulant or Cayley graphs. Absolute novelty cannot be established by search alone; an obscure special-family result could exist outside the inspected sources.
title: Exact rainbow connection of Dirac cycle powers
